orch review — audit an existing branch and land it.

Usage: orch review <branch> [options]

Audits an existing branch: no author writes a new change first, a reviewer
agent examines the diff, and the test gate and deterministic security scan run
on it. An agreed and green branch then lands on the integration branch — the
same local merge a task cycle performs, and the same guardrail and security
floors apply to it.

`orch pr <branch>` audits the same branch without that local merge, leaving the
landing to GitHub. This is the older of the two spellings and is kept for
compatibility.

Options:
  --until <goal>          What this run pursues: once, ready or merged.
                          once  = a single audit, then report.
                          ready = loop until the pull request for this branch
                                  is green and mergeable; never merge it.
                          merged = also merge the standing PR.
                          (default: once)
  --reviewer <spec>       Reviewer seat as "<agent> [model] [effort]".
  --reviewers <a,b>       Comma-separated reviewer seats.
  --cheap                 Fill the reviewer seat from cheap.role in orch.yml.
  --allow-large-scope     Sanction a deliberately large review slice.
  --no-banner             Hide the run banner.
  --detach                Run in the background; print pid, log and runId.
  --dry                   Plan only: no agent runs, nothing is written.
  --json                  Print one JSON event per line; no prose.
  --config-file <path>    Layer this YAML file over .orch/orch.yml.

Arguments: exactly one branch name.

There is no --author here: this command audits work that already has an author.

Exit codes: 0 goal reached · 1 internal error · 2 stopped at the attempt cap ·
3 blocked, a human must decide · 4 asked a human, no answer in time ·
64 usage error.

Examples:
  orch review feature/add-retry
  orch review feature/add-retry --reviewer "codex"
